sourceDate.text: 孟子 (Warring States philosopher alluded to)
太祖奉昭宗自岐還長安
太祖即位 / 梁之篡弒
唐平陽王暉 (Tang Zhangjianzhi coup era)
汴州觀察支使 under Zhu Wen at Bian
時溥 at Xuzhou until Taizu took the city
劉氏 with Shang Rang, Shi Pu, then Taizu/Xiang
李唐賓附 (appended to Zhu Zhen)

value.manner: killed in flood defeat at Qingkou

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 孟子謂「春秋無義戰」，予亦以謂五代無全臣。
units.en: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I say the Five Dynasties knew no ministers whole in loyalty.
units.literal: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I likewise hold that in the Five Dynasties there were no whole ministers.

units.zh: 無者，非無一人，蓋僅有之耳，余得死節之士三人焉。
units.en: “None” is not literally none—only a handful; I count three who died for principle.
units.literal: “None” does not mean not a single man—it means barely any; I found three men who died for principle.

units.zh: 其仕不及於二代者，各以其國系之，作梁、唐、晉、漢、周臣傳。
units.en: Men who served less than two houses I group by realm—Later Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou minister lives.
units.literal: Those whose service did not reach two dynasties, each is arranged under his state—I compose the Later Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou minister biographies.

units.zh: 其餘仕非一代，不可以國系之者，作《雜傳》。
units.en: The rest, who served more than one dynasty and cannot be tied to a single realm, go into “Miscellaneous Lives.”
units.literal: The rest, whose service was not confined to one dynasty and cannot be arranged by state, I compose “Miscellaneous Biographies.”

units.zh: 夫入於雜，誠君子之所羞，而一代之臣，未必皆可貴也，覽者詳其善惡焉。
units.en: Landing among the miscellaneous is a gentleman’s shame—yet one-dynasty ministers are not all noble; let readers judge good and evil for themselves.
units.literal: To be placed among the miscellaneous is truly what a gentleman finds shameful; yet ministers of a single dynasty are not necessarily all worthy—let readers weigh their good and evil.

units.zh: 敬翔，字子振，同州馮翊人也，自言唐平陽王暉之後。
units.en: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fengyi in Tongzhou and claimed Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui, as ancestor.
units.literal: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fengyi in Tongzhou; he claimed descent from Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui.

units.zh: 少好學，工書檄。
units.en: As a youth he studied hard and wrote excellent military dispatches.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at writing dispatches.

units.zh: 乾符中舉進士不中，乃客大梁。
units.en: During Qianfu he failed the jinshi exams and went to live as a guest at Daliang.
units.literal: In the Qianfu era he sat for the jinshi examination and failed; he then sojourned at Daliang.

units.zh: 翔同里人王發為汴州觀察支使，遂往依焉。
units.en: A fellow townsman, Wang Fa, served as aide to Bianzhou’s observation commissioner; Xiang attached himself to him.
units.literal: Wang Fa, a townsman of Xiang’s, was aide to the Bianzhou observation commissioner; Xiang went to depend on him.

units.zh: 久之，發無所薦引，翔客益窘，為人作箋刺，傳之軍中。
units.en: Fa never found him a post; Xiang’s guest life grew thin; he drafted letters and memorials for hire and passed them through the camps.
units.literal: After long time Fa had nothing with which to recommend him; Xiang’s position as guest grew desperate; he wrote letters and memorials for others and circulated them in the army.

units.zh: 太祖素不知書，翔所作皆俚俗語，太祖愛之，謂發曰：「聞君有故人，可與俱來。」
units.en: Taizu of Liang could barely read; Xiang wrote in plain soldier’s speech, and Taizu loved it. He told Fa: “I hear you have an old friend—bring him along.”
units.literal: Taizu had never known books; what Xiang wrote was all folksy language; Taizu loved it and said to Fa: “I hear you have an old acquaintance—he may come with you.”

units.zh: 翔見太祖，太祖問曰：「聞子讀《春秋》，《春秋》所記何等事？」
units.en: Xiang was brought in. Taizu asked: “They say you’ve read the Spring and Autumn—what does it record?”
units.literal: Xiang met Taizu; Taizu asked: “I hear you have read the Spring and Autumn—what affairs does the Spring and Autumn record?”

units.zh: 翔曰：「諸侯爭戰之事耳。」
units.en: Xiang said: “Lords fighting one another—that is all.”
units.literal: Xiang said: “The affairs of feudal lords competing in war, that is all.”

units.zh: 太祖曰：「其用兵之法可以為吾用乎？」
units.en: Taizu asked: “Can I use its way of war?”
units.literal: Taizu said: “Can its methods of warfare serve my use?”

units.zh: 翔曰：「兵者，應變出奇以取勝，《春秋》古法，不可用於今。」
units.en: Xiang said: “War means adapting and striking where the enemy does not expect it—the Spring and Autumn’s old ways won’t serve today.”
units.literal: Xiang said: “War is about responding to change and striking with surprise to win—the ancient methods of the Spring and Autumn cannot be used today.”

units.zh: 太祖大喜，補以軍職，非其所好，乃以為館驛巡官。
units.en: Taizu was delighted, gave him a military appointment—not what Xiang wanted—so he made him patrol officer of the post stations.
units.literal: Taizu greatly rejoiced, gave him a military post—not to his taste, so made him courier-station patrol officer.

units.zh: 太祖與蔡人戰汴郊，翔時時為太祖謀畫，多中，太祖欣然，以謂得翔之晚，動靜輒以問之。
units.en: When Taizu fought the Cai outside Bian, Xiang’s counsel usually proved right; Taizu rejoiced that he had found him so late and consulted him on every decision.
units.literal: Taizu fought the Cai at Bian’s outskirts; Xiang often plotted for him and mostly hit the mark; Taizu was pleased, saying he had found Xiang too late; in every move he asked him.

units.zh: 太祖奉昭宗自岐還長安，昭宗召翔與李振升延喜樓勞之，拜翔太府卿。
units.en: When Taizu brought Emperor Zhaozong from Qi back to Chang’an, Zhaozong summoned Xiang and Li Zhen to Ascending Bliss Tower to honor them and made Xiang Grand Treasurer.
units.literal: Taizu escorted Emperor Zhaozong from Qi back to Chang’an; Zhaozong summoned Xiang and Li Zhen to Ascending Bliss Tower to reward them and appointed Xiang Grand Treasurer.

units.zh: 初，太祖常侍殿上，昭宗意衛兵有能擒之者，乃佯為鞋結解，以顧太祖，太祖跪而結之，而左右無敢動者，太祖流汗浹背，由此稀復進見。
units.en: Early on Taizu often waited on Zhaozong in the hall; the emperor guessed the guards could grab him, so he pretended a shoe lace had loosened and looked at Taizu; Taizu knelt to tie it while no one on either side stirred; sweat ran down his back; after that he seldom came before the throne again.
units.literal: At first Taizu often attended at the throne hall; Zhaozong thought the guard soldiers could seize him; he feigned that his shoe thong had come loose and glanced at Taizu; Taizu knelt to tie it, yet none on either side dared move; Taizu sweated until his back was soaked; from this he rarely entered audience again.

units.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，宴崇勛殿，酒半起，使人召太祖入內殿，將有所托。
units.en: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang he feasted in the Hall of Honored Merit; mid-banquet he rose and summoned Taizu to the inner hall to entrust him with a charge.
units.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he held a banquet in the Hall of Honored Merit; halfway through the wine he rose and sent for Taizu to enter the inner hall, intending to entrust him with something.

units.zh: 太祖益懼，辭以疾。
units.en: Taizu was more frightened than ever and pleaded illness.
units.literal: Taizu grew still more afraid and declined on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 昭宗曰：「卿不欲來，可使敬翔來。」
units.en: Zhaozong said: “If you won’t come, send Jing Xiang.”
units.literal: Zhaozong said: “If you do not wish to come, you may send Jing Xiang.”

units.zh: 太祖遽麾翔出，翔亦佯醉去。
units.en: Taizu hurried Xiang away; Xiang also pretended to be drunk and withdrew.
units.literal: Taizu hurriedly waved Xiang out; Xiang too feigned drunkenness and left.

units.zh: 太祖已破趙匡凝，取荊、襄，遂攻淮南。
units.en: Once Taizu had defeated Zhao Kuangning and taken Jing and Xiang, he turned to attack Huainan.
units.literal: After Taizu had broken Zhao Kuangning and taken Jing and Xiang, he then attacked Huainan.

units.zh: 翔切諫，以謂新勝之兵，宜持重以養威。
units.en: Xiang urged him hard: an army just victorious should hold its weight and let its prestige ripen.
units.literal: Xiang urgently remonstrated, saying that troops fresh from victory ought to hold steady and nurture their awe.

units.zh: 太祖不聽。
units.en: Taizu would not heed him.
units.literal: Taizu would not listen.

units.zh: 兵出光州，遭大雨，幾不得進，進攻壽州，不克，而多所亡失，太祖始大悔恨。
units.en: The army marched out through Guang Prefecture, was stopped by torrential rain, then besieged Shouzhou without success and lost heavily; only then did Taizu bitterly repent.
units.literal: The army marched out through Guang Prefecture and met heavy rain, barely able to advance; advancing to attack Shouzhou, they could not take it and lost many men; Taizu at last deeply regretted it.

units.zh: 歸而忿躁，殺唐大臣幾盡，然益以翔為可信任。
units.en: Back home, furious and volatile, he slaughtered almost every Tang minister—yet trusted Xiang more than ever.
units.literal: On returning he was angry and restless and killed nearly all the Tang grandees, yet trusted Xiang all the more.

units.zh: 梁之篡弒，翔之謀為多。
units.en: When Liang seized the throne by murder, Xiang’s counsel led the way.
units.literal: In Liang’s usurpation and regicide, Xiang’s plotting was chief.

units.zh: 太祖即位，以唐樞密院故用宦者，乃改為崇政院，以翔為使。
units.en: At his accession Taizu replaced Tang’s eunuch-run Privy Council with the Chongzheng Court and made Xiang its chief.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, because Tang’s Privy Council had used eunuchs, he changed it to the Chongzheng Court and made Xiang its commissioner.

units.zh: 遷兵部尚書、金鑾殿大學士。
units.en: He rose to Minister of War and Grand Academician of the Golden Hall.
units.literal: He was promoted to Minister of War and Grand Academician of the Golden Hall.

units.zh: 翔為人深沈有大略，從太祖用兵三十餘年，細大之務必關之。
units.en: Deep, reserved, and far-sighted, Xiang followed Taizu in war for over thirty years; nothing large or small escaped his counsel.
units.literal: Xiang was deep and reserved, with great strategic vision; following Taizu in war for more than thirty years, he was consulted on matters great and small.

units.zh: 翔亦盡心勤勞，晝夜不寐，自言惟馬上乃得休息。
units.en: Xiang worked himself to the bone, barely sleeping; he said his only rest came in the saddle.
units.literal: Xiang too gave his heart in tireless labor, sleeping neither day nor night; he said only on horseback could he rest.

units.zh: 而太祖剛暴難近，有所不可，翔亦未嘗顯言，微開其端，太祖意悟，多為之改易。
units.en: Taizu was brutal and unapproachable; when Xiang disagreed he never said so outright—he would hint, Taizu would understand, and much was amended.
units.literal: Yet Taizu was harsh and hard to approach; when something could not be done, Xiang never spoke plainly; he would lightly open the matter, Taizu would grasp it, and much was changed for the better.

units.zh: 太祖破徐州，得時溥寵姬劉氏，愛幸之，劉氏故尚讓妻也，乃以妻翔。
units.en: After taking Xuzhou Taizu seized Shi Pu’s favorite concubine, Lady Liu, and doted on her; she had been Shang Rang’s wife, and Taizu gave her to Xiang in marriage.
units.literal: When Taizu took Xuzhou he obtained Shi Pu’s favored concubine, Lady Liu, whom he cherished; Lady Liu had been the wife of Shang Rang; he gave her to Xiang as wife.

units.zh: 翔已貴，劉氏猶侍太祖，出入臥內如平時，翔頗患之。
units.en: Even after Xiang had risen high, Lady Liu still served Taizu, coming and going from his bedchamber as ever; Xiang brooded over it.
units.literal: Though Xiang had risen high, Lady Liu still attended Taizu, entering and leaving his bedchamber as before; Xiang was much troubled by it.

units.zh: 劉氏誚翔曰：「爾以我嘗失身於賊乎？
units.en: Lady Liu taunted him: “Do you think I once gave myself to thieves?
units.literal: Lady Liu mocked Xiang: “Do you take me for one who once lost herself to bandits?

units.zh: 尚讓，黃家宰相；
units.en: Shang Rang was chancellor to the Huang rebels;
units.literal: Shang Rang was chancellor of the Yellow house;

units.zh: 時溥，國之忠臣。
units.en: Shi Pu was a loyal servant of the realm.
units.literal: Shi Pu was a loyal minister of the state.

units.zh: 以卿門地，猶為辱我，請從此決矣！」
units.en: Even with your rank you shame me—let us part here and now!”
units.literal: By your family standing you still disgrace me—I ask that we part from this day!”

units.zh: 翔以太祖故，謝而止之。
units.en: For Taizu’s sake Xiang apologized and kept her.
units.literal: For Taizu’s sake Xiang apologized and stopped her.

units.zh: 劉氏車服驕侈，別置典謁，交結藩鎮，權貴往往附之，寵信言事不下於翔。
units.en: Lady Liu rode in splendor, kept her own gate of audience, and courted the governors; the great often fawned on her, and Taizu heard and trusted her no less than Xiang.
units.literal: Lady Liu’s carriage and dress were proud and extravagant; she set up her own reception office, cultivated ties with military governors, and the powerful often attached themselves to her; Taizu’s favor and trust in her reports were no less than Xiang’s.

units.zh: 當時貴家，往往效之。
units.en: Fashionable houses everywhere copied her.
units.literal: Great families of the time often copied her.

units.zh: 太祖崩，友珪立，以翔先帝謀臣，懼其圖己，不欲翔居內職，乃以李振代翔為崇政使，拜翔中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: At Taizu’s death Yougui succeeded; fearing Xiang, the late emperor’s chief plotter, he kept him from inner office, put Li Zhen in charge of Chongzheng, and made Xiang Vice Director and co-equal of the Secretariat.
units.literal: When Taizu died, Yougui took the throne; because Xiang had been the late emperor’s strategist, he feared Xiang would plot against him and did not want Xiang in an inner post; he replaced Xiang with Li Zhen as Chongzheng commissioner and appointed Xiang Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal with the Secretariat.

units.zh: 翔以友珪畏己，多稱疾，未嘗省事。
units.en: Knowing Yougui feared him, Xiang often claimed sickness and never touched business.
units.literal: Because Yougui feared him, Xiang often pleaded illness and never handled affairs.

units.zh: 末帝即位，趙巖等用事，頗離間舊臣，翔愈鬱鬱不得志。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Zhao Yan and his circle took power and drove wedges among the old ministers; Xiang sank deeper into frustration.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Zhao Yan and others held power and greatly alienated the old ministers; Xiang grew ever more depressed and thwarted.

units.zh: 其後，梁盡失河北，與晉相拒楊劉，翔曰：「故時河朔半在，以先帝之武，御貔虎之臣，猶不得志於晉。
units.en: Later, after Liang lost all of Hebei and faced Jin at Yangliu, Xiang said: “Once half the north was still ours; with the late emperor’s might and his fiercest commanders, we still could not beat Jin.
units.literal: Later, when Liang had lost all of Hebei and stood against Jin at Yangliu, Xiang said: “In former days half the north still held for us; with the late emperor’s martial prowess and fierce-tiger commanders, we still could not prevail over Jin.

units.zh: 今晉日益彊，梁日益削，陛下處深宮之中，所與計事者，非其近習，則皆親戚之私，而望成事乎？
units.en: Now Jin grows stronger every day while Liang shrinks. Your Majesty sits deep in the palace, and those you consult are either personal favorites or family intimates—how can you hope to succeed?
units.literal: Now Jin grows stronger day by day and Liang weaker. Your Majesty sits deep in the palace; those with whom you counsel are either personal favorites or private kin—how can you expect success?

units.zh: 臣聞晉攻楊劉，李亞子負薪渡水，為士卒先。
units.en: I hear that when Jin struck Yangliu, Li Yazi carried firewood on his back and crossed the water ahead of his men.
units.literal: I hear that when Jin attacked Yangliu, Li Yazi shouldered firewood and crossed the water ahead of his soldiers.

units.zh: 陛下委蛇守文，以儒雅自喜，而遣賀瓌為將，豈足當彼之餘鋒乎？
units.en: Your Majesty prides himself on gentle conservatism and scholarly polish, yet sends He Gui to command—can he meet their remaining edge?
units.literal: Your Majesty prides himself on graceful conservatism and bookish refinement, yet sends He Gui as commander—can he stand against their remaining edge?

units.zh: 臣雖憊矣，受國恩深，若其乏材，願得自效。」
units.en: I am worn out, but the state’s grace runs deep; if you lack able men, I ask to serve.”
units.literal: Though I am worn out, I have received the state’s grace in full; if talent is lacking, I wish to offer myself.”

units.zh: 巖等以翔為怨言，遂不用。
units.en: Yan and his circle treated Xiang’s counsel as complaint, and he was set aside.
units.literal: Yan and the others took Xiang’s words as complaint, and he was not employed.

units.zh: 其後，王彥章敗於中都，末帝懼，召段凝於河上。
units.en: Later, when Wang Yanzhang fell at Zhongdu, the Last Emperor panicked and called Duan Ning back from the river line.
units.literal: Later, when Wang Yanzhang was defeated at Zhongdu, the Last Emperor was afraid and summoned Duan Ning from the Yellow River front.

units.zh: 是時，梁精兵悉在凝軍，凝有異志，顧望不來。
units.en: Liang’s crack troops were all with Ning; Ning had his own ambitions and hung back.
units.literal: At that time Liang’s best troops were all in Ning’s army; Ning had other designs and looked back without coming.

units.zh: 末帝遽呼翔曰：「朕居常忽卿言，今急矣，勿以為懟，卿其教我當安歸？」
units.en: The Last Emperor cried to Xiang: “I’ve ignored you too long; now it’s desperate—don’t hold a grudge—tell me where I should flee.”
units.literal: The Last Emperor hurriedly called Xiang: “I have often ignored your words; now it is urgent—do not be angry—teach me: where should I go?”

units.zh: 翔曰：「臣從先帝三十餘年，今雖為相，實朱氏老奴爾，事陛下如郎君，以臣之心，敢有所隱？
units.en: Xiang said: “I followed the late emperor thirty years; though I am chancellor I am still Zhu’s old retainer; I serve you as a steward serves his young lord—how could I hold anything back?
units.literal: Xiang said: “I have followed the late emperor more than thirty years; though I am now chancellor, I am in truth an old servant of the Zhu house; I serve Your Majesty as a young master serves his lord—in my heart, how could I hide anything?

units.zh: 陛下初用段凝，臣已爭之，今凝不來，敵勢已近，欲為陛下謀，則小人間之，必不見聽。
units.en: I fought your choice of Duan Ning from the start; now he won’t come and the foe is close—if I counsel you, slanderers will cut me off and you won’t hear me.
units.literal: When Your Majesty first used Duan Ning, I already argued against it; now Ning will not come, the enemy is near, and if I plan for Your Majesty petty men will come between us—you will surely not listen.

units.zh: 請先死，不忍見宗廟之亡！」
units.en: Let me die first—I cannot watch the ancestral temple perish!”
units.literal: Let me die first—I cannot bear to see the ancestral temple fall!”

units.zh: 君臣相向慟哭。
units.en: Emperor and minister wept face to face.
units.literal: Lord and minister faced each other and wept.

units.zh: 翔與李振俱為太祖所信任，莊宗入汴，詔赦梁群臣，李振喜謂翔曰：「有詔洗滌，將朝新君。」
units.en: Xiang and Li Zhen had both been Taizu’s confidants; when Zhuangzong took Bian, an edict pardoned Liang’s court; Li Zhen was glad and told Xiang: “We are absolved—we can bow to the new ruler.”
units.literal: Xiang and Li Zhen were both trusted by Taizu; when Zhuangzong entered Bian, an edict pardoned Liang’s ministers; Li Zhen rejoiced and said to Xiang: “There is an edict to wash us clean—we shall attend the new lord.”

units.zh: 邀翔欲俱入見。
units.en: He urged Xiang to go in with him.
units.literal: He invited Xiang to enter audience together.

units.zh: 翔夜止高頭車坊，將旦，左右報曰：「崇政李公入朝矣！」
units.en: Xiang lodged overnight at the Tall-Head Carriage Yard; at daybreak his men said: “Commissioner Li of Chongzheng has gone to audience!”
units.literal: Xiang stopped for the night at the Tall-Head Carriage Yard; near dawn his attendants reported: “Chongzheng Commissioner Li has gone to court!”

units.zh: 翔嘆曰：「李振謬為丈夫矣！
units.en: Xiang sighed: “Li Zhen has shamed the word ‘man’!
units.literal: Xiang sighed: “Li Zhen has disgraced the name of man!

units.zh: 復何面目入梁建國門乎？」
units.en: What face have I left to pass through Liang’s Founding Gate?”
units.literal: What face have I to enter Liang’s Founding Gate?”

units.zh: 乃自經而卒。
units.en: He hanged himself.
units.literal: He hanged himself and died.

units.zh: 朱珍
units.en: Zhu Zhen
units.literal: Zhu Zhen

units.zh: 〈（李唐賓附）〉
units.en: (with Li Tangbin appended)〉
units.literal: (Li Tangbin appended)〉

units.zh: 朱珍，徐州豐人也。
units.en: Zhu Zhen came from Feng in Xuzhou.
units.literal: Zhu Zhen was a native of Feng in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 少與龐師古等俱從梁太祖為盜。
units.en: As a young man he rode with Pang Shigu and the rest under Taizu of Liang as outlaws.
units.literal: In youth he followed Pang Shigu and others with Taizu of Liang as bandits.

units.zh: 珍為將，善治軍選士，太祖初鎮宣武，珍為太祖創立軍制，選將練兵甚有法。
units.en: As a commander Zhen excelled at discipline and choosing men; when Taizu first held Xuanwu, Zhen built his army system, picking officers and drilling troops with real art.
units.literal: Zhen as a general was skilled at governing armies and selecting men; when Taizu first held Xuanwu, Zhen for him established the army system, choosing commanders and drilling troops with great method.

units.zh: 太祖得諸將所募兵及佗降兵，皆以屬珍，珍選將五十餘人，皆可用。
units.en: Every recruit the generals raised and every surrendered unit Taizu handed to Zhen; Zhen picked out more than fifty commanders, all of them good.
units.literal: The troops the various generals had recruited and other surrendered soldiers Taizu all put under Zhen; Zhen chose more than fifty commanders, all usable.

units.zh: 梁敗黃巢、破秦宗權、東並兗鄆，未嘗不在戰中，而常勇出諸將。
units.en: Through Liang’s defeat of Huang Chao, breakup of Qin Zongquan, and eastward swallowing of Yan and Yanzhou, Zhen was always in the fight and often outshone the rest in courage.
units.literal: Liang defeated Huang Chao, broke Qin Zongquan, and marched east to swallow Yan and Yanzhou—Zhen was never absent from battle and was often braver than the other generals.

units.zh: 太祖與晉王東逐黃巢，還過汴，館之上源驛，太祖使珍夜以兵攻之，晉王亡去，珍悉殺其麾下兵。
units.en: When Taizu and the Prince of Jin chased Huang Chao east and passed Bian, they stopped at Shangyuan Post; Taizu sent Zhen by night to strike the Jin prince; the prince escaped, and Zhen slaughtered his escort.
units.literal: Taizu and the Prince of Jin drove Huang Chao east; returning they passed Bian and lodged at Shangyuan Post; Taizu sent Zhen by night with troops to attack him; the Prince of Jin fled; Zhen killed all his followers.

units.zh: 義成軍亂，逐安師儒，師儒奔梁。
units.en: Yicheng mutinied, expelled An Shiru, and Shiru fled to Liang.
units.literal: The Yicheng army mutinied, drove out An Shiru, and Shiru fled to Liang.

units.zh: 太祖遣珍以兵趨滑州，道遇大雪，珍趣兵疾馳，一夕至城下，遂乘其城。
units.en: Taizu sent Zhen racing toward Hua Province; snow fell hard on the march, but Zhen drove the men at a gallop and reached the walls in a single night, seizing the city by surprise.
units.literal: Taizu sent Zhen with troops to rush Hua Province; on the road they met heavy snow; Zhen urged the army at full speed and in one night reached below the walls, then took the city by surprise.

units.zh: 義成軍以為方雪，不意梁兵來，不為備，遂下之。
units.en: Yicheng thought the snow meant no attack; unprepared, they fell.
units.literal: The Yicheng army thought it was still snowing and did not expect Liang troops; they made no preparations and were taken.

units.zh: 秦宗權遣盧瑭、張至等攻梁，是時梁兵尚少，數為宗權所困。
units.en: Qin Zongquan sent Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, and others against Liang; Liang’s forces were still small and often pinned by Zongquan.
units.literal: Qin Zongquan sent Lu Tang and Zhang Zhi and others to attack Liang; at that time Liang’s troops were still few and were often hard pressed by Zongquan.

units.zh: 太祖乃拜珍淄州刺史，募兵於淄青。
units.en: Taizu made Zhen prefect of Zi and sent him to raise troops in Zi and Qing.
units.literal: Taizu then appointed Zhen prefect of Zi and had him recruit troops in Zi and Qing.

units.zh: 珍偏將張仁遇白珍曰：「軍中有犯令者，請先斬而後白。」
units.en: Zhen’s lieutenant Zhang Renyu said: “If anyone in the ranks breaks orders, let me cut off his head first and report after.”
units.literal: Zhen’s lieutenant Zhang Renyu told Zhen: “When there are men in the army who break orders, let me behead them first and report afterward.”

units.zh: 珍曰：「偏將欲專殺邪？」
units.en: Zhen said: “Does a lieutenant mean to kill at will?”
units.literal: Zhen said: “Does a lieutenant mean to kill on his own authority?”

units.zh: 立斬仁遇以徇軍，軍中皆感悅。
units.en: He had Renyu executed on the spot before the troops; the army was awed and won over.
units.literal: He immediately beheaded Renyu to display to the army; the army was all moved and pleased.

units.zh: 珍得所募兵萬餘以歸，太祖大喜曰：「賊在吾郊，若踐吾麥，奈何！
units.en: Zhen came back with more than ten thousand fresh recruits; Taizu was overjoyed: “The rebels are at our gates—if they tread our wheat, what then!
units.literal: Zhen returned with more than ten thousand recruited troops; Taizu greatly rejoiced and said: “The bandits are at our suburbs—if they trample our wheat, what then!

units.zh: 今珍至，吾事濟矣！
units.en: Now Zhen is here, my cause is saved!
units.literal: Now that Zhen has come, my affair is settled!

units.zh: 且賊方息兵養勇，度吾兵少，而未知珍來，謂吾不過堅守而已，宜出其不意以擊之。」
units.en: And they are resting and regrouping, counting our small force and not knowing Zhen has arrived—they think we’ll only sit tight; we should hit them unawares.”
units.literal: Moreover the bandits are just resting their troops and gathering strength; they gauge our few numbers and do not yet know Zhen has come—they think we can only hold firm; we should strike them where they do not expect it.”

units.zh: 乃出兵擊敗至等，宗權由此敗亡，而梁軍威大振，以得珍兵故也。
units.en: He marched out, smashed Zhang Zhi and the rest, and Zongquan collapsed; Liang’s prestige soared—all from the army Zhen brought home.
units.literal: He then sent out troops, defeated Zhang Zhi and the others, and Zongquan from this was broken and destroyed; Liang’s military prestige greatly rose—all because of the troops Zhen brought.

units.zh: 珍從太祖攻朱宣，取曹州，執其刺史丘弘禮。
units.en: Zhen followed Taizu against Zhu Xuan, took Caozhou, and seized its prefect Qiu Hongli.
units.literal: Zhen followed Taizu in attacking Zhu Xuan, took Caozhou, and captured its prefect Qiu Hongli.

units.zh: 又取濮州，刺史朱裕奔於鄆州。
units.en: He took Puzhou too; its prefect Zhu Yu fled to Yanzhou.
units.literal: He also took Puzhou; its prefect Zhu Yu fled to Yanzhou.

units.zh: 太祖乃還汴，留珍攻鄆州。
units.en: Taizu went back to Bian and left Zhen to besiege Yanzhou.
units.literal: Taizu then returned to Bian and left Zhen to besiege Yanzhou.

units.zh: 珍去鄆二十里，遣精兵挑之，鄆人不出。
units.en: Twenty li from Yan, Zhen sent elite troops to taunt them; Yan’s garrison stayed shut.
units.literal: Twenty li from Yan, Zhen sent picked troops to provoke them; the men of Yan would not come out.

units.zh: 朱裕詐為降書，陰使人召珍，約開門為內應。
units.en: Zhu Yu faked a surrender and secretly called Zhen, promising to open the gate from within.
units.literal: Zhu Yu forged a surrender letter and secretly sent men to summon Zhen, agreeing to open the gate as inside help.

units.zh: 珍信之，夜率其兵叩鄆城門，朱裕登陴，開門內珍軍，珍軍已入甕城而垂門發，鄆人從城上磔石以投之，珍軍皆死甕城中，珍僅以身免，太祖不之責也。
units.en: Zhen believed him; at night he led his men to the gate; Zhu Yu appeared on the wall, opened it, and let them into the barbican—then dropped the outer gate; Yan’s defenders rained stones from above; Zhen’s force died to the last man in the trap; Zhen alone got out alive; Taizu did not punish him.
units.literal: Zhen believed it; by night he led his troops to knock at Yan’s gate; Zhu Yu mounted the wall, opened the gate, and admitted Zhen’s army; once Zhen’s troops had entered the barbican the gate was dropped; the men of Yan hurled stones from the wall; Zhen’s army all died in the barbican; Zhen barely escaped with his life; Taizu did not blame him.

units.zh: 魏博軍亂，囚樂彥貞。
units.en: Weibo mutinied and seized Yue Yanzhen.
units.literal: The Weibo army mutinied and imprisoned Yue Yanzhen.

units.zh: 太祖遣珍救魏，珍破黎陽、臨河、李固，分遣聶金、範居實等略澶州，殺魏豹子軍二千於臨黃。
units.en: Taizu sent Zhen to relieve Wei; Zhen took Liyang, Linhe, and Liguo, and detached Nie Jin, Fan Jushi, and others to overrun Cao Province, slaughtering two thousand of Wei’s Leopard-Son troops at Linhuang.
units.literal: Taizu sent Zhen to rescue Wei; Zhen broke Liyang, Linhe, and Liguo, and separately sent Nie Jin, Fan Jushi, and others to overrun Cao Province, killing two thousand of Wei’s Leopard-Son Army at Linhuang.

units.zh: 珍威振河朔。
units.en: Zhen’s name shook the lands north of the river.
units.literal: Zhen’s prestige shook the north of the Yellow River.

units.zh: 魏人殺彥貞，珍乃還。
units.en: Weibo killed Yanzhen; Zhen withdrew.
units.literal: The men of Wei killed Yanzhen; Zhen then returned.

units.zh: 梁攻徐州，遣珍先攻下豐縣，又敗時溥於吳康，與李唐賓等屯蕭縣。
units.en: In Liang’s assault on Xuzhou, Zhen first took Feng County, then beat Shi Pu at Wukang and camped at Xiao County with Li Tangbin and the rest.
units.literal: When Liang attacked Xuzhou, they sent Zhen first to take Feng County, then defeated Shi Pu at Wukang, and with Li Tangbin and others encamped at Xiao County.

units.zh: 唐賓者，陜人也。
units.en: Tangbin came from Shan.
units.literal: Tangbin was a native of Shan.

units.zh: 初為尚讓偏將，與太祖戰尉氏門，為太祖所敗，唐賓乃降梁。
units.en: He had been Shang Rang’s lieutenant; beaten by Taizu at the Weishi Gate, he surrendered to Liang.
units.literal: At first he was a lieutenant of Shang Rang; fighting Taizu at the Weishi Gate, he was defeated by Taizu and then surrendered to Liang.

units.zh: 梁兵攻掠四方，唐賓常與珍俱，與珍威名略等，而驍勇過之，珍戰每小卻，唐賓佐之乃大勝。
units.en: On Liang’s campaigns Tangbin usually fought beside Zhen; his name almost equaled Zhen’s, and he was the bolder fighter—whenever Zhen’s line buckled, Tangbin’s push turned defeat into rout.
units.literal: As Liang’s armies raided on every side, Tangbin often marched with Zhen; his fame nearly matched Zhen’s, yet he was even fiercer in battle; whenever Zhen’s fight faltered a little, Tangbin’s support turned it into a great victory.

units.zh: 珍嘗私迎其家置軍中，太祖疑珍有異志，遣唐賓伺察之。
units.en: Zhen once quietly moved his family into camp; Taizu suspected disloyalty and sent Tangbin to spy on him.
units.literal: Zhen once secretly brought his family into camp; Taizu suspected Zhen of other designs and sent Tangbin to watch him.

units.zh: 珍與唐賓不協，唐賓不能忍，夜走還宣武，珍單騎追之，交訴太祖前。
units.en: Zhen and Tangbin clashed; Tangbin could not bear it and fled by night to Xuanyi; Zhen chased him alone, and both argued their case before Taizu.
units.literal: Zhen and Tangbin did not get along; Tangbin could not endure it and fled by night back to Xuanyi; Zhen rode alone in pursuit and both pleaded their case before Taizu.

units.zh: 太祖兩惜其材，為和解之。
units.en: Taizu prized both men and patched peace between them.
units.literal: Taizu valued both men’s talent and reconciled them.

units.zh: 珍屯蕭縣，聞太祖將至，戒軍中治館廄以待。
units.en: Camped at Xiao County, Zhen heard Taizu was on his way and had the camp ready quarters and stables.
units.literal: Zhen encamped at Xiao County; hearing Taizu was coming, he ordered the army to prepare lodges and stables in welcome.

units.zh: 唐賓部將嚴郊治廄失期，軍吏督之，郊訴於唐賓，唐賓以讓珍，珍怒，拔劍而起，唐賓拂衣就珍，珍即斬之，遣使者告唐賓反。
units.en: Tangbin’s lieutenant Yan Jiao missed the deadline on the stables; the clerks drove him; Jiao appealed to Tangbin, who blamed Zhen; Zhen flew into a rage, drew his sword, and when Tangbin strode up to him, killed him on the spot, then sent word that Tangbin had rebelled.
units.literal: Tangbin’s lieutenant Yan Jiao was late preparing the stables; the army clerks pressed him; Jiao complained to Tangbin; Tangbin reproached Zhen; Zhen in anger drew his sword and rose; Tangbin brushed his robe and went to Zhen; Zhen at once cut him down and sent a messenger reporting that Tangbin had rebelled.

units.zh: 使者晨至梁，敬翔恐太祖暴怒不可測，乃匿使者，至夜而見之，謂雖有所發，必須明旦，冀得少緩其事而圖之。
units.en: The messenger reached Bian at dawn; Jing Xiang, dreading Taizu’s unpredictable fury, hid him until night and said that whatever had happened must wait for morning—buying time to soften the blow and work a way out.
units.literal: The messenger reached Liang at dawn; Jing Xiang feared Taizu’s violent rage could not be measured; he hid the messenger and saw him only at night, saying that even if something had happened it must wait until morning, hoping to soften the affair a little and find a way through.

units.zh: 既夕，乃引珍使者入見，太祖大驚，然已夜矣，不能有所發，翔因從容為太祖畫。
units.en: At dusk he brought Zhu Zhen’s messenger before Taizu. Taizu was shaken, but night had fallen and nothing could be done yet; Xiang calmly drew up a plan for him.
units.literal: Evening came; he then brought Zhu Zhen’s messenger in to see Taizu. Taizu was greatly alarmed, but night had already fallen and nothing could be done at once; Xiang then calmly laid out a plan for Taizu.

units.zh: 明日，佯收唐賓妻子下獄。
units.en: The next day he feigned arresting Li Tangbin’s wife and children and threw them in prison.
units.literal: The next day he pretended to arrest Li Tangbin’s wife and children and put them in prison.

units.zh: 因如珍軍，去蕭一舍，珍迎謁，太祖命武士執之。
units.en: Then he rode to Zhen’s camp, halting one post short of Xiao. Zhen came out to greet him; Taizu ordered his men to seize him.
units.literal: Then he went to Zhu Zhen’s camp, stopping one lodge short of Xiao. Zhen came out to receive him; Taizu ordered warriors to seize him.

units.zh: 諸將霍存等十餘人叩頭救珍，太祖大怒，舉胡床擲之曰：「方珍殺唐賓時，獨不救之邪！」
units.en: Generals Huo Cun and a dozen others kowtowed to beg for Zhen. Taizu in a rage hurled a camp stool at them and cried: “When Zhen killed Li Tangbin, where were you then!”
units.literal: The generals Huo Cun and more than ten others prostrated themselves to plead for Zhen. Taizu in great anger threw a folding chair at them and said: “When Zhen killed Li Tangbin, why did you alone not save him!”

units.zh: 存等退，珍遂縊死。
units.en: They withdrew; Zhen hanged himself.
units.literal: Huo Cun and the others withdrew; Zhen then hanged himself.

units.zh: 龐師古
units.en: Pang Shigu
units.literal: Pang Shigu

units.zh: 龐師古，曹州南華人也，初名從。
units.en: Pang Shigu came from Nanhua in Caozhou; he had first been named Cong.
units.literal: Pang Shigu was a native of Nanhua in Caozhou; his original name was Cong.

units.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，初得馬五百匹為騎兵，乃以師古將之，從破黃巢、秦宗權，皆有功。
units.en: When Taizu of Liang held Xuanwu, he raised five hundred horses into a cavalry force and gave Shigu command; under him Shigu helped break Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan.
units.literal: When Emperor Taizu of Liang held Xuanwu, he first obtained five hundred horses for cavalry and put Shigu in command; following him he broke Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan, earning merit in both campaigns.

units.zh: 太祖攻時溥未下，留兵屬師古守之，師古取其宿遷，進屯呂梁。
units.en: Taizu besieged Shi Pu without success and left Shigu to hold the line. Shigu took Suqian and pushed forward to Luliang.
units.literal: Taizu attacked Shi Pu but could not take him; he left troops under Shigu to hold the field. Shigu seized Suqian and advanced to camp at Luliang.

units.zh: 溥以兵二萬出戰，師古敗之，斬首二千級。
units.en: Pu marched out with twenty thousand men; Shigu routed him and took two thousand heads.
units.literal: Pu came out with twenty thousand men; Shigu defeated him and took two thousand heads.

units.zh: 孫儒逐楊行密，取揚州，淮南大亂，太祖遣師古渡淮攻儒，為儒所敗。
units.en: Sun Ru drove Yang Xingmi from Yangzhou and threw Huainan into chaos. Taizu sent Shigu across the Huai against him—and Ru beat him back.
units.literal: Sun Ru drove out Yang Xingmi and took Yangzhou; Huainan fell into great disorder. Taizu sent Shigu across the Huai to attack Ru, but Ru defeated him.

units.zh: 是時，朱珍、李唐賓已死，師古與霍存分將其兵。
units.en: Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin were already dead; Shigu and Huo Cun split their commands between them.
units.literal: By then Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin were dead; Shigu and Huo Cun divided their commands among themselves.

units.zh: 郴王友裕攻徐州，朱瑾以兵救時溥，友裕敗溥於石佛山，瑾收余兵去。
units.en: Prince of Chen Youyu attacked Xuzhou. Zhu Jin marched to save Shi Pu. Youyu crushed Pu at Mount Shifo; Jin gathered what was left and withdrew.
units.literal: Prince of Chen Youyu attacked Xuzhou. Zhu Jin came with troops to rescue Shi Pu. Youyu defeated Pu at Mount Shifo; Jin gathered the remnant force and withdrew.

units.zh: 太祖以友裕可追而不追，奪其兵以屬師古。
units.en: Taizu judged that Youyu could have pursued but had not; he stripped him of his army and handed it to Shigu.
units.literal: Taizu thought Youyu could have pursued but did not; he stripped him of command and gave the troops to Shigu.

units.zh: 師古攻破徐州，斬溥，太祖表師古徐州留後。
units.en: Shigu stormed Xuzhou, killed Pu, and Taizu memorialized to make him its military governor.
units.literal: Shigu stormed Xuzhou, killed Pu, and Taizu memorialized to make Shigu military governor of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 梁兵攻鄆州，臨濟水，師古徹木為橋，夜以中軍先濟。
units.en: Liang attacked Yanzhou and reached the Ji River. Shigu felled trees for a bridge and at night led the center army across first.
units.literal: Liang forces attacked Yanzhou and came to the Ji River. Shigu tore down timber for a bridge and at night led the center army across first.

units.zh: 朱宣走中都，見殺。
units.en: Zhu Xuan fled to Zhongdu and was killed.
units.literal: Zhu Xuan fled to Zhongdu and was killed.

units.zh: 太祖已下兗、鄆，乃遣師古與葛從周攻楊行密於淮南，師古出清口，從周出安豐。
units.en: Once Yan and Yun had fallen, Taizu sent Shigu and Ge Congzhou against Yang Xingmi in Huainan—Shigu from Qingkou, Congzhou from Anfeng.
units.literal: After Taizu had taken Yan and Yun, he sent Shigu and Ge Congzhou against Yang Xingmi in Huainan. Shigu marched from Qingkou; Congzhou from Anfeng.

units.zh: 師古自其微時事太祖，為人謹甚，未嘗離左右，及為將出兵，必受方略以行，軍中非太祖命，不妄動。
units.en: Shigu had served Taizu from the beginning, careful and close, never far from his side. As a field commander he moved only on orders; without Taizu’s word the army did not stir.
units.literal: From his humble beginnings Shigu had served Taizu. Meticulous by nature, he never left his side. Once he became a general and took the field he always acted on received strategy; without Taizu’s orders the army did not stir.

units.zh: 師古營清口，地勢卑，或請就高為柵，師古以非太祖命不聽。
units.en: At Qingkou Shigu camped on low ground. Some urged him to fortify higher ground; he refused—Taizu had not ordered it.
units.literal: Shigu encamped at Qingkou on low ground. Some urged him to build palisades on higher ground; Shigu refused because he had no order from Taizu.

units.zh: 淮人決水浸之，請者告曰：「淮人決河，上流水至矣！」
units.en: The Huai men broke the dikes to flood the camp. The adviser cried: “They have opened the river—the flood is coming!”
units.literal: The Huai people opened the dikes to flood them. The adviser cried: “The Huai have broken the river—the upstream flood is coming!”

units.zh: 師古以為搖動士卒，立斬之。
units.en: Shigu judged it would panic the ranks and had him cut down at once.
units.literal: Shigu thought this would shake the troops’ morale and had him executed on the spot.

units.zh: 已而水至，兵不能戰，遂見殺。
units.en: The water came; the army could not fight, and Shigu was killed.
units.literal: Soon the water came; the army could not fight, and Shigu was killed.

units.zh: 嗚呼，兵之勝敗，豈易言哉！
units.en: Alas—who can speak lightly of victory and defeat in war!
units.literal: Alas—can victory and defeat in war be spoken of lightly!

units.zh: 梁兵強於天下，而吳人號為輕弱，然師古再舉擊吳，輒再敗以死。
units.en: Liang’s armies were the strongest under heaven; Wu was counted weak—yet Shigu struck twice, and twice died in defeat.
units.literal: Liang’s army was strongest in the realm, while Wu was called light and weak; yet Shigu twice struck Wu and twice met defeat and death.

units.zh: 其後太祖自將出光山，攻壽春，然亦敗也。
units.en: Later Taizu himself marched from Guangshan against Shouchun—and lost there too.
units.literal: Later Taizu personally led troops from Guangshan to attack Shouchun—and was defeated as well.

units.zh: 蓋自高駢死，唐以梁兼統淮南，遂與孫、楊爭，凡三十年間，三舉而三敗。
units.en: From Gao Pian’s death Tang entrusted Huainan to Liang, and for thirty years Liang contended with Sun and Yang—three campaigns, three defeats.
units.literal: From Gao Pian’s death, Tang had Liang hold Huainan jointly; thus they contended with Sun and Yang. In thirty years, three campaigns and three defeats.

units.zh: 以至強遭至弱而如此，此其不可以理得也。
units.en: That the mightiest should fall so to the weakest—reason alone cannot explain it.
units.literal: That the mightiest should meet the weakest and suffer so—this cannot be grasped by reason alone.

units.zh: 兵法固有以寡而敗眾、以弱而勝強者，顧吳豈足以知之哉！
units.en: The art of war knows times when the few beat the many and the weak overcome the strong—but did Wu know that?
units.literal: Military craft does hold cases where the few defeat the many, the weak overcome the strong—but could Wu alone have known this?

units.zh: 豈非適與其機會邪？
units.en: Was it not simply that fortune fell their way?
units.literal: Was it not simply that fortune fell their way?

units.zh: 故曰：「兵者兇器，戰者危事也。」
units.en: Thus it is said: “Arms are ill-omened tools; war is perilous business.”
units.literal: Thus it is said: “Arms are ill-omened tools; battle is perilous business.”

units.zh: 可不慎哉！
units.en: Handle them with care!
units.literal: One must be cautious!

units.zh: 葛從周
units.en: Ge Congzhou
units.literal: Ge Congzhou

units.zh: 葛從周，字通美，濮州甄城人也。
units.en: Ge Congzhou, styled Tongmei, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
units.literal: Ge Congzhou, styled Tongmei, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.

units.zh: 少從黃巢，敗降梁。
units.en: In youth he followed Huang Chao; when the nest fell he submitted to Liang.
units.literal: In youth he followed Huang Chao; when Huang was defeated he submitted to Liang.

units.zh: 從太祖攻蔡州，太祖墜馬，從周扶太祖復騎，與敵步鬥傷面，身被數瘡，偏將張延壽從旁擊之，從周得與太祖俱去。
units.en: At Caizhou Taizu was thrown from his horse. Congzhou helped him remount, fought on foot with the enemy, took wounds to the face and body, and with Zhang Yanshou’s help fought free with Taizu.
units.literal: Following Taizu against Caizhou, Taizu fell from his horse. Congzhou helped him remount; fighting on foot with the enemy he was wounded in the face and bore many cuts. The deputy general Zhang Yanshou struck from the side, and Congzhou escaped with Taizu.

units.zh: 太祖盡黜諸將，獨用從周、延壽為大將。
units.en: Taizu dismissed every other general and kept only Congzhou and Yanshou as his chief commanders.
units.literal: Taizu dismissed all the other generals and kept only Congzhou and Yanshou as chief commanders.

units.zh: 秦宗權掠地潁、亳，及梁兵戰於焦夷，從周獲其將王涓一人。
units.en: When Qin Zongquan raided Ying and Bo, Congzhou fought him at Jiaoyi and captured his general Wang Juan.
units.literal: Qin Zongquan raided Ying and Bo; when Liang forces fought at Jiaoyi, Congzhou captured one of his generals, Wang Juan.

units.zh: 從朱珍收兵淄青，遇東兵輒戰，珍得兵歸，從周功為多。
units.en: With Zhu Zhen he gathered troops in Ziqing and fought every eastern force they met. When Zhen returned, Congzhou’s share of the credit was greatest.
units.literal: Following Zhu Zhen to gather troops in Ziqing, he fought eastern troops whenever he met them. When Zhen returned with the soldiers, Congzhou’s merit was greatest.

units.zh: 張全義襲李罕之於河陽，罕之奔晉，召晉兵以攻全義，全義乞兵於梁，太祖遣從周、丁會等救之，敗晉兵於沇河。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi struck Li Hanzhi at Heyang. Hanzhi fled to Jin and called Jin armies against Quanyi. Taizu sent Congzhou and Ding Hui to his aid and beat the Jin at the Yan River.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi attacked Li Hanzhi at Heyang. Hanzhi fled to Jin and summoned Jin troops against Quanyi. Quanyi begged Liang for aid; Taizu sent Congzhou, Ding Hui, and others to rescue him and defeated Jin forces at the Yan River.

units.zh: 潞州馮霸殺晉守將李克恭以降梁，太祖遣從周入潞州，晉兵攻之，從周不能守，走河陽。
units.en: At Luzhou Feng Ba killed the Jin commander Li Kegong and surrendered to Liang. Taizu sent Congzhou in; Jin attacked; Congzhou could not hold and fled to Heyang.
units.literal: At Luzhou, Feng Ba killed the Jin garrison commander Li Kegong and surrendered to Liang. Taizu sent Congzhou into Luzhou; Jin attacked; Congzhou could not hold and fled to Heyang.

units.zh: 太祖攻魏，從周與丁會先下黎陽、臨河，會太祖於內黃，敗魏兵於永定橋。
units.en: Taizu attacked Wei. Congzhou and Ding Hui first took Liyang and Linhe, joined Taizu at Neihuang, and broke Wei at Yongding Bridge.
units.literal: Taizu attacked Wei; Congzhou and Ding Hui first took Liyang and Linhe, joined Taizu at Neihuang, and defeated Wei forces at Yongding Bridge.

units.zh: 從丁會攻宿州，以水浸其城，遂破之。
units.en: With Ding Hui at Suzhou he flooded the city and took it.
units.literal: Following Ding Hui against Suzhou, he flooded the city with water and took it.

units.zh: 太祖攻朱瑾於兗州，未下，留從周圍之，瑾閉壁不出，從周詐言救兵至，陽避之高吳，夜半潛還城下，瑾以謂從周已去，乃出兵收外壕，從周掩擊之，殺千餘人。
units.en: Taizu besieged Zhu Jin at Yanzhou without success and left Congzhou to hold the siege. Jin shut the walls. Congzhou feigned that relief had come and openly withdrew toward Gaowu; at midnight he stole back. Jin thought him gone and sent men to clear the outer ditch—Congzhou sprang the trap and killed more than a thousand.
units.literal: Taizu besieged Zhu Jin at Yanzhou but could not take him; he left Congzhou to invest the city. Jin shut the gates and would not come out. Congzhou feigned that relief had arrived and openly withdrew toward Gaowu; at midnight he slipped back below the walls. Jin thought Congzhou had gone and sent troops to take the outer moat; Congzhou ambushed them and killed more than a thousand.

units.zh: 晉攻魏，魏人求救，太祖遣侯言救魏，言築壘於洹水。
units.en: Jin attacked Wei. Taizu sent Hou Yan to relieve it; Yan built fortifications on the Huan River.
units.literal: Jin attacked Wei; Wei pleaded for help. Taizu sent Hou Yan to relieve Wei; Yan built fortifications at the Huan River.

units.zh: 太祖怒言不出戰，遣從周代言。
units.en: Taizu raged that Yan would not fight and sent Congzhou to replace him.
units.literal: Taizu was angry that Yan would not fight and sent Congzhou to replace him.

units.zh: 從周至軍，益閉壘不出，而鑿三暗門以待，晉兵攻之，從周以精兵自暗門出擊，敗晉王兵。
units.en: Congzhou arrived, shut the works tighter still, and cut three hidden sally ports. When Jin attacked he led elite troops out through them and beat the Prince of Jin’s army.
units.literal: Congzhou reached the army, closed the works even tighter, and cut three hidden gates in readiness. When Jin attacked, Congzhou led elite troops out through the hidden gates and defeated the Prince of Jin’s army.

units.zh: 晉王怒，自將擊從周，從周雖大敗，而梁兵擒其子落落，送於魏，斬之。
units.en: The Prince of Jin came in person. Congzhou was badly beaten, but Liang captured his son Luoluo, sent him to Wei, and had him executed.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin in rage led the attack himself. Though Congzhou suffered a great defeat, Liang forces captured his son Luoluo, sent him to Wei, and executed him.

units.zh: 遂徙攻鄆州，擒朱宣於中都，又攻兗州，走朱瑾。
units.en: He then turned on Yanzhou, seized Zhu Xuan at Zhongdu, and drove Zhu Jin from Yan.
units.literal: Then he turned to attack Yanzhou, seized Zhu Xuan at Zhongdu, and again attacked Yanzhou, driving out Zhu Jin.

units.zh: 太祖表從周兗州留後，以兗、鄆兵攻淮南，出安豐，會龐師古於清口。
units.en: Taizu made Congzhou military governor of Yan and sent Yan and Yun troops against Huainan from Anfeng to join Pang Shigu at Qingkou.
units.literal: Taizu memorialized to make Congzhou military governor of Yanzhou and sent Yan and Yun troops against Huainan, marching from Anfeng to join Pang Shigu at Qingkou.

units.zh: 從周行至濠州，聞師古死，遽還，至渒河將渡而淮兵追之，從周亦大敗。
units.en: At Haozhou Congzhou heard Shigu was dead and turned back in haste. At the Bei River, as he was about to cross, Huai troops caught him—and he too was routed.
units.literal: Congzhou reached Haozhou, heard Shigu was dead, and hurried back. At the Bei River he was about to cross when Huai troops pursued; Congzhou also suffered a great defeat.

units.zh: 是時，晉兵出山東攻相、衛，太祖遣從周略地山東，下洺州，斬其刺史邢善益；
units.en: Jin marched out of Shandong against Xiang and Wei. Taizu sent Congzhou to sweep Shandong—he took Mingzhou and killed its prefect Xing Shanyi;
units.literal: At this time Jin troops came out of Shandong to attack Xiang and Wei. Taizu sent Congzhou to sweep Shandong, took Mingzhou, and killed its prefect Xing Shanyi;

units.zh: 又下邢州，走其刺史馬師素；
units.en: then took Xingzhou and routed its prefect Ma Shisu;
units.literal: then took Xingzhou and routed its prefect Ma Shisu;

units.zh: 又下磁州，殺其刺史袁奉滔。
units.en: then took Cizhou and killed its prefect Yuan Fengtao.
units.literal: then took Cizhou and killed its prefect Yuan Fengtao.

units.zh: 五日而下三州。
units.en: Three prefectures in five days.
units.literal: In five days he took three prefectures.

units.zh: 太祖乃表從周兼邢州留後。
units.en: Taizu then made Congzhou military governor of Xing as well.
units.literal: Taizu then memorialized to make Congzhou also military governor of Xingzhou.

units.zh: 劉仁恭攻魏，已屠貝州，羅紹威求救於梁，從周會太祖救魏，入於魏州。
units.en: Liu Rengong attacked Wei and had already sacked Beizhou. Luo Shaowei begged Liang for aid; Congzhou joined Taizu, relieved Wei, and entered Weizhou.
units.literal: Liu Rengong attacked Wei and had already slaughtered Beizhou. Luo Shaowei begged Liang for help; Congzhou joined Taizu to relieve Wei and entered Weizhou.

units.zh: 燕兵攻館陶門，從周以五百騎出戰，曰：「大敵在前，何可返顧！」
units.en: Yan attacked the Guantao Gate. Congzhou rode out with five hundred horse and cried: “The enemy is ahead—who looks back!”
units.literal: Yan forces attacked the Guantao Gate. Congzhou rode out with five hundred cavalry and said: “A great enemy lies ahead—how can we look back!”

units.zh: 使閉門而後戰。
units.en: He had the gates shut behind him and fought.
units.literal: He had the gates shut behind him and then fought.

units.zh: 破其八柵，燕兵走，追至於臨清，擁之御河，溺死者甚眾。
units.en: He broke eight palisades; the Yan fled. Pursuit reached Linqing and drove them into the Yu River—many drowned.
units.literal: He broke eight palisades; Yan troops fled. Pursuit reached Linqing and drove them into the Yu River; very many drowned.

units.zh: 太祖以從周為宣義行軍司馬。
units.en: Taizu made Congzhou campaign marshal of Xuanyi.
units.literal: Taizu made Congzhou campaign marshal of Xuanyi.

units.zh: 太祖遣從周攻劉守文於滄州，以蔣暉監其軍。
units.en: Taizu sent Congzhou against Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and put Jiang Hui over the army as supervisor.
units.literal: Taizu sent Congzhou to attack Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and placed Jiang Hui to supervise the army.

units.zh: 守文求救於其父仁恭，仁恭以燕兵救之，暉語諸將曰：「吾王以我監諸將，今燕兵來，不可迎戰，宜縱其入城，聚食倉廩，使兩困而後取之。」
units.en: Shouwen called on his father Rengong, who marched with Yan troops. Hui told the generals: “I was sent to watch you. Yan is coming—do not fight. Let them into the city to eat from the granaries; when both sides are spent, take them.”
units.literal: Shouwen begged his father Rengong for help; Rengong brought Yan troops to his aid. Hui told the generals: “Our lord set me to oversee you. Now Yan troops come—we must not meet them in battle. Let them enter the city to gather provisions from the granaries; when both sides are exhausted, then take them.”

units.zh: 諸將頗以為然。
units.en: Most of the generals agreed.
units.literal: The generals mostly agreed.

units.zh: 從周怒曰：「兵在上將，豈監軍所得言！
units.en: Congzhou snapped: “Command rests with the general—since when does a supervisor give orders!
units.literal: Congzhou angrily said: “Command belongs to the chief general—what business has a supervisor to speak!

units.zh: 且暉之言乃常談爾，勝敗之機在吾心，暉豈足以知之！」
units.en: And Hui’s counsel is common talk. Victory and defeat are mine to read—what does Hui know of it!”
units.literal: Besides, Hui’s words are empty talk. The moment of victory or defeat lies in my heart—how could Hui know it!”

units.zh: 乃勒兵逆仁恭於乾寧，戰於老鴉堤，仁恭大敗，斬首三萬餘級，獲其將馬慎交等百餘人，馬三千匹。
units.en: He marched to meet Rengong at Qianning and fought at Old Crow Embankment. Rengong was shattered—thirty thousand heads, more than a hundred captives including Ma Shenjiao, and three thousand horses.
units.literal: He then led troops to intercept Rengong at Qianning and fought at Old Crow Embankment. Rengong was utterly defeated: more than thirty thousand heads, over a hundred captives including the general Ma Shenjiao, and three thousand horses.

units.zh: 是時，守文亦求救於晉，晉為攻邢、洺以牽之，從周遽還，敗晉兵於青山。
units.en: Shouwen also called on Jin, which struck Xing and Ming to pull Congzhou away. Congzhou turned back and beat the Jin at Qingshan.
units.literal: At this time Shouwen also begged Jin for help; Jin attacked Xing and Ming to draw Congzhou off. Congzhou hurried back and defeated Jin troops at Qingshan.

units.zh: 遂從太祖攻鎮州，下臨城，王熔乞盟，太祖表從周泰寧軍節度使。
units.en: He followed Taizu against Zhenzhou and took Lincheng. Wang Rong sued for peace; Taizu made Congzhou military governor of Taining.
units.literal: Then he followed Taizu against Zhenzhou, took Lincheng. Wang Rong asked for peace; Taizu memorialized to make Congzhou military governor of Taining.

units.zh: 從氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。
units.en: Congzhou joined Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan but could not take it.
units.literal: Congzhou joined Shi Shuzong in attacking Taiyuan of Jin but could not take it.

units.zh: 梁兵西攻鳳翔，青州王師範遣其將劉鄩襲兗州，從周家屬為鄩所得，厚遇之而不殺。
units.en: Liang marched west on Fengxiang. Wang Shifan of Qingzhou sent Liu Yun to strike Yanzhou; Yun captured Congzhou’s family, treated them generously, and spared their lives.
units.literal: Liang troops marched west against Fengxiang. Wang Shifan of Qingzhou sent his general Liu Yun to raid Yanzhou; Congzhou’s family were captured by Yun, who treated them well and did not kill them.

units.zh: 太祖還自鳳翔，乃遣從周攻鄩，從周卒招降鄩。
units.en: Taizu returned from Fengxiang and sent Congzhou against Yun; Congzhou finally talked Yun into surrender.
units.literal: When Taizu returned from Fengxiang he sent Congzhou against Yun; Congzhou finally persuaded Yun to surrender.

units.zh: 太祖即位，拜左金吾衞上將軍，以疾致仕，拜右衞上將軍，居于偃師。
units.en: At Taizu’s accession Congzhou became Left General of the Golden Crow Guard; he later retired for illness, was made Right Guard General, and lived at Yanshi.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he made Congzhou Left General of the Golden Crow Guard, then retired on account of illness and was made Right Guard General, living at Yanshi.

units.zh: 末帝即位，拜昭義軍節度使、陳留郡王，食其俸于家。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Congzhou was made military governor of the Zhaoyi Army and Prince of Chenliu, with salary paid at home.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Congzhou was made military governor of the Zhaoyi Army and Prince of Chenliu, drawing his salary at home.

units.zh: 卒，贈太尉。
units.en: He died and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 霍存，洺州曲周人也。
units.en: Huo Cun came from Quzhou in Mingzhou.
units.literal: Huo Cun was a native of Quzhou in Mingzhou.

units.zh: 少從黃巢，巢敗，存乃降梁。
units.en: In youth he followed Huang Chao; when the nest fell he submitted to Liang.
units.literal: In youth he followed Huang Chao; when the nest fell, Cun submitted to Liang.

units.zh: 存為將驍勇，善騎射。
units.en: As a commander he was fierce and skilled in mounted archery.
units.literal: As a commander Cun was fierce and brave, skilled in mounted archery.

units.zh: 秦宗權攻汴，存以三千人夜破張至柵，又以騎兵破秦賢，殺三千人，敗至於赤岡。
units.en: When Qin Zongquan struck Bian, Cun with three thousand men broke Zhang Zhi’s palisade by night, then with cavalry broke Qin Xian, killed three thousand, and chased the rout to Chigang.
units.literal: Qin Zongquan attacked Bian. Cun with three thousand men broke Zhang Zhi’s palisade by night; again with cavalry he broke Qin Xian, killing three thousand, and chased the defeated to Chigang.

units.zh: 從朱珍掠淄青、龐師古攻時溥，皆有功。
units.en: With Zhu Zhen in Ziqing and Pang Shigu against Shi Pu he won credit in both campaigns.
units.literal: Following Zhu Zhen in raiding Ziqing and Pang Shigu in attacking Shi Pu, he earned merit in both.

units.zh: 朱珍與李唐賓俱死，乃以龐師古代珍、存代唐賓以攻溥，破碭山，存獲其將石君和等五十人。
units.en: After Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin died, Pang Shigu took Zhen’s command and Cun took Tangbin’s to attack Pu. They broke Mount Dang; Cun captured fifty men, including the general Shi Junhe.
units.literal: When Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin both died, Pang Shigu replaced Zhen and Cun replaced Tangbin to attack Pu. They broke Mount Dang; Cun captured fifty men including the general Shi Junhe.

units.zh: 梁攻宿州，葛從周引水浸之，丁會與存戰城下，遂下之。
units.en: At Suzhou Ge Congzhou flooded the city; Ding Hui and Cun fought below the walls and took it.
units.literal: Liang attacked Suzhou. Ge Congzhou flooded it with water; Ding Hui and Cun fought beneath the walls and took the city.

units.zh: 從攻潞州，與晉人遇，戰馬牢川，存入則當其前，出則為其殿，晉人卻，遂東攻魏，取淇門，殺三千人。
units.en: At Luzhou they met the Jin at Malao Stream. Cun led on the advance and covered the retreat. The Jin fell back; they turned east on Wei, took Qimen, and killed three thousand.
units.literal: In the attack on Luzhou they met Jin forces and fought at Malao Stream. Cun on entering took the van; on withdrawal covered the rear. Jin withdrew; they then marched east against Wei, took Qimen, and killed three thousand.

units.zh: 梁得曹州，太祖以存為刺史，兼諸軍都指揮使。
units.en: When Liang took Caozhou, Taizu made Cun its prefect and commander-in-chief of all armies.
units.literal: When Liang took Caozhou, Taizu made Cun its prefect and also commander-in-chief of all armies.

units.zh: 梁攻鄆州，朱瑾來救，梁諸將或勸太祖縱瑾入鄆，耗其食，堅圍勿戰，以此可俱弊。
units.en: Liang besieged Yanzhou; Zhu Jin came to its aid. Some generals urged Taizu to let Jin into Yan, drain his grain, and hold the siege without fighting until both sides were spent.
units.literal: Liang attacked Yanzhou; Zhu Jin came to the rescue. Some Liang generals urged Taizu to let Jin enter Yan, drain his supplies, hold the siege and not fight—to wear both sides down.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「瑾來必與時溥俱，不若遣存邀之。」
units.en: Taizu said: “Jin will come with Shi Pu—send Cun to intercept them.”
units.literal: Taizu said: “When Jin comes he will surely be with Shi Pu—better send Cun to intercept them.”

units.zh: 存伏兵蕭縣，已而瑾果與溥俱出迷離，存發伏擊之，遂敗瑾等於石佛山，存中流矢卒。
units.en: Cun hid men at Xiao County. Jin and Pu came out together at Mili; Cun sprang the trap and crushed them at Mount Shifo. He took an arrow and died.
units.literal: Cun hid troops at Xiao County. Presently Jin did come out with Pu at Mili; Cun sprang the ambush and defeated Jin and the rest at Mount Shifo. Cun took an arrow in flight and died.

units.zh: 太祖已即位，閱騎兵於繁臺，顧諸將曰：「使霍存在，豈勞吾親閱邪！
units.en: After Taizu took the throne he reviewed cavalry at Fanzang Terrace and told his generals: “If Huo Cun were alive, would I need to do this myself!
units.literal: After Taizu had ascended the throne he reviewed cavalry at Fanzang Terrace and said to the generals: “If Huo Cun were alive, would I need to review them myself!

units.zh: 諸君寧復思之乎？」
units.en: Do you still remember him?”
units.literal: Do you still remember him?”

units.zh: 佗日語又如此。
units.en: Another day he said the same again.
units.literal: On another day he spoke this way again.

units.zh: 張存敬
units.en: Zhang Cunjing
units.literal: Zhang Cunjing

units.zh: 張存敬，譙郡人也。
units.en: Zhang Cunjing came from Qiao commandery.
units.literal: Zhang Cunjing was a native of Qiao commandery.

units.zh: 為人剛直有膽勇，少事梁太祖為將，善因危窘出奇計。
units.en: Upright and bold, he served Taizu of Liang as a young commander and had a gift for desperate stratagems in tight corners.
units.literal: Upright and bold, in youth he served Emperor Taizu of Liang as a commander and excelled at desperate stratagems in peril.

units.zh: 李罕之與晉人攻張全義於河陽，太祖遣存敬與丁會等救之，罕之解圍去。
units.en: Li Hanzhi and the Jin besieged Zhang Quanyi at Heyang. Taizu sent Cunjing with Ding Hui to relieve him; Hanzhi broke off and withdrew.
units.literal: Li Hanzhi with Jin forces besieged Zhang Quanyi at Heyang. Taizu sent Cunjing with Ding Hui and others to relieve him; Hanzhi lifted the siege and left.

units.zh: 太祖以存敬為諸軍都虞候。
units.en: Taizu made Cunjing chief adjutant of all armies.
units.literal: Taizu made Cunjing chief adjutant of all armies.

units.zh: 太祖攻徐、兗，以存敬為行營都指揮使。
units.en: Taizu attacked Xu and Yan and made Cunjing commander of the field headquarters.
units.literal: Taizu attacked Xu and Yan and made Cunjing commander-in-chief of the field headquarters.

units.zh: 從葛從周攻滄州，敗劉仁恭於老鴉堤。
units.en: With Ge Congzhou at Cangzhou he helped defeat Liu Rengong at Old Crow Embankment.
units.literal: Following Ge Congzhou against Cangzhou, he defeated Liu Rengong at Old Crow Embankment.

units.zh: 還攻王熔於鎮州，入其城中，取其馬牛萬計。
units.en: Turning on Wang Rong at Zhenzhou he entered the city and took tens of thousands of horses and cattle.
units.literal: Returning to attack Wang Rong at Zhenzhou, he entered the city and took tens of thousands of horses and cattle.

units.zh: 遷宋州刺史。
units.en: He was made prefect of Song.
units.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Song.

units.zh: 復從諸將攻幽州，存敬取其瀛、莫、祁、景四州。
units.en: Again with the generals against Youzhou, he took Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing.
units.literal: Again following the generals against Youzhou, Cunjing took the four prefectures of Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing.

units.zh: 梁攻定州，與王處直戰懷德驛，大敗之，枕屍十餘里。
units.en: At Dingzhou he fought Wang Chuzhi at Huade Post and broke him—corpses lay stacked for more than ten li.
units.literal: Liang attacked Dingzhou and fought Wang Chuzhi at Huade Post; they were utterly defeated, corpses stacked for more than ten li.

units.zh: 梁已下鎮、定，乃遣存敬攻王珂於河中，存敬出含山，下晉、絳二州，珂降於梁。
units.en: After Zhen and Ding fell, Taizu sent Cunjing against Wang Ke at Hezhong. Cunjing came out from Hanshan, took Jin and Jiang, and Ke submitted to Liang.
units.literal: After Liang had taken Zhen and Ding, Taizu sent Cunjing against Wang Ke at Hezhong. Cunjing came out from Hanshan, took Jin and Jiang prefectures; Ke submitted to Liang.

units.zh: 太祖表存敬護國軍留後，復徙宋州刺史，未至，卒於河中，贈太傅。
units.en: Taizu made Cunjing military governor of Huguo, then transferred him to Song—but he died at Hezhong before he arrived and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Taizu memorialized to make Cunjing military governor of Huguo; then transferred him again to prefect of Song. Before he arrived he died at Hezhong and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 存敬子仁穎、仁願。
units.en: Cunjing’s sons were Renying and Renyuan.
units.literal: Cunjing’s sons were Renying and Renyuan.

units.zh: 仁願有孝行，存敬卒，事其兄仁穎，出必告，反必面，如事父之禮。
units.en: Renyuan was filial. After Cunjing died he served his elder brother Renying—going out he announced it, returning he reported face to face, as to a father.
units.literal: Renyuan was filial. After Cunjing died he served his elder brother Renying—going out he always announced it; returning he always reported in face to face, as one would serve a father.

units.zh: 仁願曉法令，事梁、唐、晉，常為大理卿，卒，贈秘書監。
units.en: Renyuan knew the law. Under Liang, Tang, and Jin he often served as chief judge of the supreme court. He died and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Renyuan knew the law. Serving Liang, Tang, and Jin, he was often chief judge of the supreme court. He died and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 符道昭
units.en: Fu Daozhao
units.literal: Fu Daozhao

units.zh: 符道昭，蔡州人也。
units.en: Fu Daozhao came from Caizhou.
units.literal: Fu Daozhao was a native of Caizhou.

units.zh: 為秦宗權騎將，宗權敗，道昭流落無所依，後依鳳翔李茂貞，茂貞愛之，養以為子，名繼遠。
units.en: He was a cavalry commander under Qin Zongquan. When Zongquan fell, Daozhao wandered without a patron until he joined Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, who favored him, adopted him as a son, and named him Jiyuan.
units.literal: He served Qin Zongquan as a cavalry commander. When Zongquan fell, Daozhao was adrift with nowhere to turn; later he attached himself to Li Maozhen of Fengxiang. Maozhen favored him, adopted him as a son, and gave him the name Jiyuan.

units.zh: 梁攻茂貞，道昭與梁兵戰，屢敗，乃歸梁，太祖表道昭秦州節度使，以亂不果行。
units.en: When Liang struck Maozhen, Daozhao fought Liang again and again and lost; he then submitted to Liang. Taizu memorialized to make him military governor of Qinzhou, but the chaos kept the appointment from taking effect.
units.literal: When Liang attacked Maozhen, Daozhao fought Liang troops repeatedly and was often defeated; he then submitted to Liang. Taizu memorialized to make Daozhao military governor of Qinzhou, but because of disorder the appointment was not carried out.

units.zh: 太祖為元帥，初開府，而李周彝以鄜州降，以為左司馬，擇右司馬難其人，及得道昭，乃授之。
units.en: When Taizu became commander-in-chief and first opened headquarters, Li Zhouyi surrendered Yan Prefecture and was made Left Chief of Staff. A worthy Right Chief of Staff was hard to find; when Daozhao came forward, he received the post.
units.literal: When Taizu became commander-in-chief and first opened his headquarters, Li Zhouyi surrendered Yan Prefecture; Taizu made Zhouyi Left Chief of Staff. Finding the right man for Right Chief of Staff was difficult, and when Daozhao became available he was given the post.

units.zh: 羅紹威將誅其牙兵，惡魏兵彊，未敢發，求梁為助。
units.en: Luo Shaowei meant to wipe out his yajun retainers but feared Wei’s strength and held back until he asked Liang for help.
units.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to exterminate his yajun retainers, he feared the strength of Wei troops and did not dare act; he asked Liang for help.

units.zh: 太祖乃悉發魏兵使攻燕，而遣馬嗣勳助紹威誅牙兵。
units.en: Taizu sent all Wei troops against Yan and dispatched Ma Sixun to help Shaowei slaughter the yajun.
units.literal: Taizu then sent out all Wei troops to attack Yan and dispatched Ma Sixun to help Shaowei execute the yajun.

units.zh: 牙兵已誅，魏兵在外者聞之皆亂，魏將左行遷據歷亭、史仁遇據高唐以叛，道昭等從太祖悉破之。
units.en: Once the yajun were dead, Wei troops abroad mutinied. Zuo Xingqian seized Liting and Shi Renyu Gaotang in revolt; Daozhao followed Taizu and crushed them all.
units.literal: After the yajun were executed, Wei troops still in the field heard the news and all rose in disorder. Wei generals Zuo Xingqian seized Liting and Shi Renyu seized Gaotang in rebellion; Daozhao and the others followed Taizu and broke them all.

units.zh: 道昭為將，勇於犯敵而少成筭，每戰先發，多敗，而周彝等繼之乃勝。
units.en: Daozhao fought boldly but planned poorly; he always struck first, often lost, and only when Zhouyi and others followed did the day turn.
units.literal: As a commander Daozhao was bold in striking the enemy but poor at calculation; he always led the attack and was often defeated, yet Zhouyi and the others who followed would then win.

units.zh: 開平元年與康懷英等攻潞州，築夾城為蚰蜒塹以圍之，逾年不能下，晉兵攻破夾城，道昭戰死。
units.en: In Kaiping 1 he joined Kang Huaiying against Luzhou, building twin encampments linked by a centipede trench. After more than a year the city still held; Jin broke the encirclement and Daozhao fell in battle.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaiping he joined Kang Huaiying and others in attacking Luzhou, building the twin cities into a centipede trench to besiege it. More than a year passed without success; Jin troops broke the twin cities and Daozhao died in battle.

units.zh: 劉捍
units.en: Liu Han
units.literal: Liu Han

units.zh: 劉捍，開封人也。
units.en: Liu Han came from Kaifeng.
units.literal: Liu Han was a native of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 為人明敏有威儀，善擯贊。
units.en: Clever and dignified, he excelled at advocacy.
units.literal: He was clever and clear-minded, with a dignified bearing, and skilled at advocacy.

units.zh: 太祖初鎮宣武，以為客將，使從朱珍募兵淄青。
units.en: When Taizu first secured Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and sent him with Zhu Zhen to raise troops in Ziqing.
units.literal: When Taizu first took command of Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and had him follow Zhu Zhen to recruit troops in Ziqing.

units.zh: 太祖北攻鎮州，與王鎔和，遣捍見鎔，鎔軍未知梁意，方嚴兵，捍馳一騎入城中，諭鎔以太祖意，鎔乃聽命。
units.en: When Taizu marched north on Zhenzhou and made peace with Wang Rong, he sent Han to see him. Rong’s army did not know Liang’s intent and stood on alert; Han rode alone into the city, explained Taizu’s purpose, and Rong submitted.
units.literal: When Taizu marched north against Zhenzhou and made peace with Wang Rong, he sent Han to see Rong. Rong’s army did not yet know Liang’s intent and stood in strict readiness; Han galloped alone into the city, explained Taizu’s purpose to Rong, and Rong then obeyed.

units.zh: 梁兵攻定州，降王處直，捍復以一騎入慰城中。
units.en: When Liang took Dingzhou and Wang Chuzhi submitted, Han again rode in alone to reassure the city.
units.literal: When Liang troops attacked Dingzhou and Wang Chuzhi submitted, Han again entered the city alone on horseback to reassure the people within.

units.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，遣捍入見李茂貞計事。
units.en: Besieging Fengxiang, Taizu sent Han in to confer with Li Maozhen.
units.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he sent Han in to see Li Maozhen and discuss affairs.

units.zh: 唐昭宗召見，問梁軍中事，稱旨，賜以錦袍，拜登州刺史，賜號「迎鑾毅勇功臣」。
units.en: Emperor Zhaozong summoned him, questioned him on Liang’s armies, liked his answers, gave him a brocade robe, made him prefect of Deng, and granted the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.”
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong of Tang summoned him, questioned him on Liang military affairs, found his answers pleasing, bestowed a brocade robe on him, made him prefect of Dengzhou, and granted the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.”

units.zh: 梁兵攻淮南，遣捍先之淮口，築馬頭下浮橋以渡梁兵。
units.en: Attacking Huainan, Taizu sent Han ahead to the Huai mouth to build a floating bridge below Matou for Liang troops.
units.literal: When Liang troops attacked Huainan, Taizu sent Han ahead to the Huai mouth to build a floating bridge below Matou to ferry Liang forces across.

units.zh: 太祖出光山攻壽州，又使捍作浮橋于淮北，以渡歸師。
units.en: Marching from Guangshan against Shouzhou, Taizu again had Han build a floating bridge north of the Huai for the returning army.
units.literal: When Taizu marched out from Guangshan to attack Shouzhou, he again had Han build a floating bridge north of the Huai to ferry the returning army.

units.zh: 拜宋州刺史。
units.en: He was made prefect of Song.
units.literal: He was appointed prefect of Song.

units.zh: 太祖即位，遷左天武指揮使、元從親軍都虞候、左龍虎統軍，出為佑國軍留後。
units.en: At Taizu’s accession Han became commander of the Left Heavenly Martial Guard, chief adjutant of the Founding Personal Army, and Left Dragon-Tiger commander, then went out as acting governor of the Youguo Army.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Han was transferred to commander of the Left Heavenly Martial Guard, chief adjutant of the Founding Personal Army, and Left Dragon-Tiger commander, then sent out as acting military governor of the Youguo Army.

units.zh: 同州劉知俊反，以賂誘捍將吏，執捍而去，知俊械之，送于李茂貞，見殺。
units.en: When Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled, he bribed Han’s officers, seized him, fettered him, and sent him to Li Maozhen, who had him killed.
units.literal: When Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled, he bribed Han’s officers and seized Han. Zhijun put him in fetters and sent him to Li Maozhen, where he was killed.

units.zh: 太祖哀之，贈捍太傅。
units.en: Taizu mourned him and posthumously made Han Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Taizu mourned him and posthumously made Han Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 寇彥卿
units.en: Kou Yanqing
units.literal: Kou Yanqing

units.zh: 寇彥卿，字俊臣，開封人也。
units.en: Kou Yanqing, styled Junchen, came from Kaifeng.
units.literal: Kou Yanqing, styled Junchen, was a native of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 世事宣武軍為牙將。
units.en: His family had served the Xuanwu Army as staff officers for generations.
units.literal: For generations his family served the Xuanwu Army as military officers.

units.zh: 太祖初就鎮，以為通引官，累遷右長直都指揮使，領洺州刺史。
units.en: When Taizu first secured the circuit command, he made Yanqing a staff liaison, raised him to Right Chief of the Long Direct Guard, and gave him Ming Prefecture.
units.literal: When Taizu first took command of the circuit, he made Yanqing a liaison officer, repeatedly promoted him to Right Chief of the Long Direct Guard, and had him hold Ming Prefecture as governor.

units.zh: 羅紹威將誅牙軍，太祖遣彥卿之魏計事，彥卿陰為紹威計畫，乃悉誅牙軍。
units.en: When Luo Shaowei meant to wipe out the yajun retainers, Taizu sent Yanqing to Wei to plan. Yanqing secretly laid out Shaowei’s scheme, and the yajun were slaughtered to the last man.
units.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to exterminate the yajun, Taizu sent Yanqing to Wei to discuss affairs; Yanqing secretly devised plans for Shaowei, and thereby the yajun were all executed.

units.zh: 彥卿身長八尺，隆準方面，語音如鐘，工騎射，好書史，善伺太祖意，動作皆如旨。
units.en: Eight chi tall, high-nosed and square-jawed, Yanqing spoke in a voice like a bell. He rode and shot with skill, loved history, and read Taizu’s mood so well that word and deed always landed where the Founder wanted.
units.literal: Yanqing stood eight chi tall, with a high nose and square face; his voice rang like a bell. Skilled at mounted archery, he loved books and history, and excelled at reading Taizu’s intentions—his words and deeds always matched the master’s will.

units.zh: 太祖嘗曰：「敬翔、劉捍、寇彥卿皆天為我生之。」
units.en: Taizu once said: “Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing—Heaven gave them all to me.”
units.literal: Taizu once said: “Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing—all three Heaven bore for me.”

units.zh: 其愛之如此。
units.en: Such was his love for Yanqing.
units.literal: His affection for Yanqing was such.

units.zh: 賜以所乘愛馬「一丈烏」。
units.en: He gave him his own cherished mount, “Ten-foot Black.”
units.literal: He bestowed on him the beloved horse he rode, named “Ten-foot Black.”

units.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，以彥卿為都排陣使，彥卿乘烏馳突陣前，太祖目之曰：「真神將也！」
units.en: Besieging Fengxiang, Taizu made Yanqing formation marshal. Yanqing spurred the black steed straight into the enemy line. Taizu watched and cried: “There rides a god of war!”
units.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he made Yanqing overall formation marshal. Yanqing rode the black steed in a charge at the front of the array. Taizu pointed at him and said: “A true divine general!”

units.zh: 初，太祖與崔胤謀，欲遷都洛陽，而昭宗不許。
units.en: Early on Taizu and Cui Yin schemed to shift the capital to Luoyang, but Emperor Zhaozong refused.
units.literal: At first Taizu plotted with Cui Yin to move the capital to Luoyang, but Emperor Zhaozong would not agree.

units.zh: 其後昭宗奔於鳳翔，太祖以兵圍之，昭宗既出，明年，太祖以兵至河中，遣彥卿奉表迫請遷都。
units.en: Then the emperor fled to Fengxiang and Taizu besieged him. Once he was extracted, Taizu marched to Hezhong the next year and sent Yanqing with a memorial to force the move east.
units.literal: Later the emperor fled to Fengxiang; Taizu besieged him with troops. After the emperor came out, the following year Taizu marched to Hezhong and sent Yanqing to present a memorial pressing for relocation of the capital.

units.zh: 彥卿因悉驅徙長安居人以東，人皆拆屋為筏，浮渭而下，道路號哭，仰天大罵曰：「國賊崔胤、朱溫使我至此！」
units.en: Yanqing then drove the people of Chang’an east. They ripped houses apart for rafts and drifted down the Wei; the roads rang with weeping and curses heavenward: “The traitors Cui Yin and Zhu Wen brought us to this!”
units.literal: Yanqing then drove all residents of Chang’an eastward. People tore down houses to build rafts and floated down the Wei; on the roads they wailed, cursed heaven, and shouted: “The traitors Cui Yin and Zhu Wen have brought us to this!”

units.zh: 昭宗亦顧瞻陵廟，傍徨不忍去，謂其左右為俚語云：「紇幹山頭凍死雀，何不飛去生處樂。」
units.en: Emperor Zhaozong looked back at the imperial tombs, lingered, and could not bear to go. He told his attendants a folk verse: “On Hegu hilltop sparrows freeze to death—why not fly back to where you were born and take your joy?”
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong also looked back at the tombs and temples, hesitating, unable to leave, and told his attendants a vulgar saying: “On Hegu hill the sparrows freeze to death—why not fly away to where you were born and know joy.”

units.zh: 相與泣下沾襟。
units.en: They wept together until their robes were wet.
units.literal: Together they wept until their lapels were soaked.

units.zh: 昭宗行至華州，遣人告太祖以何皇后有娠，願留華州待冬而行。
units.en: At Huazhou the emperor sent word that Empress He was pregnant and begged to wait there until winter before moving on.
units.literal: When the emperor reached Huazhou, he sent word to Taizu that Empress He was with child and asked to remain at Huazhou until winter before traveling.

units.zh: 太祖大怒，顧彥卿曰：「汝往趣官家來，不可一日留也。」
units.en: Taizu flew into a rage and turned to Yanqing: “Ride to Huazhou and drag the emperor out—not one day more.”
units.literal: Taizu was furious and turned to Yanqing: “You go and hurry the Son of Heaven along—not one day may he remain.”

units.zh: 彥卿復馳至華，即日迫昭宗上道。
units.en: Yanqing galloped back to Huazhou and that same day drove the emperor onto the road.
units.literal: Yanqing galloped again to Huazhou and that same day forced the emperor onto the road.

units.zh: 太祖即位，拜彥卿感化軍節度使。
units.en: At Taizu’s accession Yanqing was made military governor of the Ganhua Army.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he made Yanqing military governor of the Ganhua Army.

units.zh: 歲餘，召為左金吾衞大將軍，充金吾街仗使。
units.en: After a year he recalled Yanqing as Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and director of the Jinwu street guard.
units.literal: After more than a year he summoned Yanqing as Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and made him director of the Jinwu street guard.

units.zh: 彥卿晨朝至天津橋，民梁現不避道，前驅捽現投橋上石欄以死。
units.en: One morning on his way to court Yanqing reached Tianjin Bridge. A commoner named Liang Xian failed to clear the road; the vanguard seized him and smashed him against the bridge railing to his death.
units.literal: On a morning audience Yanqing reached Tianjin Bridge. A commoner named Liang Xian did not yield the road, and the vanguard seized him and dashed him against the bridge railing to his death.

units.zh: 彥卿見太祖自首，太祖惜之，詔彥卿以錢償現家以贖罪。
units.en: Yanqing went to Taizu and confessed. Taizu pitied him and ordered Yanqing to pay Liang Xian’s family to redeem the offense.
units.literal: Yanqing went to Taizu and confessed. Taizu pitied him and ordered Yanqing to pay money to Liang Xian’s family to redeem his offense.

units.zh: 御史司憲崔沂劾奏彥卿，請論如法，太祖不得已，責授彥卿左衞中郎將。
units.en: Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi impeached Yanqing and demanded legal punishment. Taizu had no choice and demoted him to Left Guard Captain.
units.literal: Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi memorialized against Yanqing, asking that he be punished by law. Taizu had no choice and demoted Yanqing to Left Guard Captain.

units.zh: 復拜相州防禦使，遷河陽節度使。
units.en: He was again made Defender of Xiangzhou, then transferred to military governor of Heyang.
units.literal: Yanqing was again appointed Defender of Xiangzhou and transferred to military governor of Heyang.

units.zh: 太祖遇弒，彥卿出太祖畫像事之如生，嘗對客語先朝，必涕泗交下。
units.en: After Taizu was murdered, Yanqing hung his portrait and tended it as though he still lived; when he spoke of the old reign before guests, tears always streamed down.
units.literal: When Taizu was assassinated, Yanqing brought out Taizu’s portrait and served it as though he were still alive; speaking of the former court before guests he always wept profusely.

units.zh: 末帝即位，徙鎮威勝。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Yanqing was transferred to Weisheng command.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Yanqing was transferred to Weisheng.

units.zh: 彥卿明敏善事人，而怙寵作威，好誅殺，多猜忌。
units.en: Clever and skilled at winning favor, Yanqing still bullied others on the strength of his patronage, loved killing, and lived in suspicion.
units.literal: Yanqing was clever and adept at pleasing others, yet he relied on favor to throw his weight around, loved executions, and was much given to suspicion.

units.zh: 卒於鎮，年五十七。
units.en: He died in command, aged fifty-seven.
units.literal: He died at his post, aged fifty-seven.
